title: Finding your first customers through direct, consent-based outreach
audience: Any home-service operator, including solo operators, starting or growing a business.
learningOutcomes: Write an initial message that offers help without an immediate sale
Book a discovery call and ask about the customer's problem

instruction.heading: Outreach is a numbers game with a human face
instruction.body: Most first customers come from many conversations. Plan a daily routine of outreach, follow-up and engagement. Expect to send far more messages than you receive replies.

instruction.heading: Open with value, not a pitch
instruction.body: A short message that names something specific about the person and offers a no-cost check or tip is a more relevant opening than a sales pitch. The ACCC's 2026 media release on unsolicited selling reports that many approaches were pressured or misleading, so a relevant message that clearly names who is writing stands apart. Ask what is hardest for them right now.

instruction.heading: Discovery call first
instruction.body: On the call, ask about the problem, what they have tried, what it cost and what they would change. Listen more than you talk. Offer a proposal only when they ask, or when you have confirmed the problem and your fit.

instruction.heading: Consent and spam rules
instruction.body: Unsolicited commercial electronic messages in Australia are regulated by the federal Spam Act 2003 (Cth). The basis for sending is consent, which can be express or, in narrow cases, inferred. An existing relationship is not, on its own, permission to send marketing: inferred consent needs an ongoing relationship with marketing tied to it, and it does not cover a message sent just after a purchase. Each message must identify the sender and include a free unsubscribe that works for at least 30 days and is honoured within 5 working days. A business email address published online does not by itself allow marketing messages. Check current ACMA guidance and the Act's text before any bulk messaging. Do not buy or scrape contact lists.

instruction.heading: Follow-up and referrals
instruction.body: Follow up on a planned schedule over a few weeks, spaced out, and stop once the messages agreed in advance have been sent. Ask every customer for a referral and a review, with their consent.

procedure: Choose a daily time block for outreach and follow-up.
Write two or three message versions and track which get replies.
Send only to people in your target group who have a reason to hear from you.
Book discovery calls and record the problem in their words.
Follow up on a set schedule and stop after the agreed number of messages.
Ask each customer for a referral and a review.

workedExamples.situation: A pool technician sends messages to property managers who have posted about a pool problem. Some reply, and some of those replies lead to a call.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which step should be improved first?
workedExamples.reasoning: Replies show the message is getting attention. Improve the discovery call (listening and problem questions) and track follow-up, rather than increasing volume.

commonErrors.prevention: Offer help first and ask a question.

commonErrors.error: Messaging people without consent or an unsubscribe option
commonErrors.prevention: Send only to people who have consented, and include a working opt-out.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check state or territory rules before acting.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: Consistent, consent-based outreach beats one large campaign.
Use discovery calls to find the problem before offering a service.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which first message is most likely to get a reply?
options: A specific, no-pitch offer of help with a question
A long list of your prices and your discounts
A demand that they book now by Friday afternoon
A message to every person in a directory

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a discovery call focus on?
options: Your prices, your discounts and the dates
The customer's problem and what they have tried
Your awards and your press coverage list
Your competitors' pricing sheet, shared line by line

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the Spam Act 2003 (Cth) generally require for commercial electronic messages?
options: The number of pages in your quote template
The colour of your van and the font on your invoices
Consent, sender identification and an unsubscribe facility
The name of the customer's dog

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say to check before any bulk messaging?
options: The number of likes on your last post

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Read via summary tool: marketing messages need the recipient's consent (express consent is the best practice; inferred consent is less reliable); each message must identify the sender accurately; each commercial message must include a free, working unsubscribe facility that is honoured within 5 working days. Publisher: Australian Communications and Media Authority. The Spam Act 2003 text itself was not read in this pass.
